summary: Round 2 is a real step up: fog at noon is now a convincing milky high-key medium with correct distance dissolve, night is a moonlit dark blue with stars and grey-blue clouds, shadows are soft and clean, every engine hook (setSun/setHemisphere/setFog/setFogHeight/setEnvironment/setExposure/addMaterialHook/setSunModulation/uWetness) is wired, world.env is fully published, 0 console errors/warnings, perf far inside budget, and time/weather jumps snap on the first frame. It still fails the AAA bar on the two things the spec calls out hardest. Golden hour is not gorgeous: the frame goes uniformly khaki/tan, the sun reads as a clipped white blob with a flat streak instead of a warm disc, and shadows are neutral grey-brown with no warm/cool split. Clouds still read as a ceiling of flat pancake slabs with dead-flat brown bases at 18:33 and as low-frequency blurry smudges at 13:00; CS2 cumulus (cs2_09) are crisp, domed and individually shaped. New bug: under fog the PMREM probe still shows a blue sky, so the pool (and any glossy surface) reflects saturated blue against a white sky. Good indie with obvious gaps; not yet something a CS2 player accepts without comment.

issues.description: Golden hour is muddy, not gorgeous. Whole frame collapses to khaki/tan (grass desaturated across the lower half), the sun between the right towers is a clipped white blob plus a flat white streak instead of a warm orange disc, and plaza shadows are neutral grey-brown with no cool counterpart to the amber key.
issues.evidence: shots/critic/environment/r2gh.png: sun blob ~(960-1010, 285-315), streak toward (830,640); plaza shadows (300-800, 330-500); khaki ground (0-1280, 330-720). Compare reference/cs2_09.jpg warm haze + saturated sky + long soft shadows.
issues.suggestion: Below ~8 deg sun altitude clamp sun colour near 2200K (~1.0,0.55,0.25) and cap disc radiance so the tonemapper lands orange not white; push hemisphere sky term toward zenith blue (~0.35,0.45,0.75) so shadow regions go cool; stop tinting the hemisphere ground term tan (keep grass albedo saturation); apply warm Mie aerial perspective only in the sun-facing hemisphere and keep it cool elsewhere. Verify: shadowed plaza pixels should have b > r, lit plaza r > b.

issues.description: Volumetric clouds still read as slabs. At 18:33 the deck is a row of flat pancakes with a shared dead-flat brown base plane; at 13:00 the clouds are low-frequency blurry smudges with soft mushy edges and no crisp cauliflower detail.
issues.evidence: shots/critic/environment/r2gh.png top band (0-1280, 55-160); shots/critic/environment/r2_environment_hero_13.png top-left (0-450, 60-200). Clouds.js resolutionScale high=0.45.
issues.suggestion: Vary base height per column (+/-15% via the weather map) so bases are not one plane; add a high-frequency 32^3 Worley erosion at 3-4x base frequency applied on coverage^0.5 near edges; raise high-quality resolution scale to >=0.6 with the temporal accumulation carrying the cost; light bases at golden hour from the sun-side horizon sky sample (orange) instead of a uniform brown ambient.

issues.description: Reflection probe/sky mismatch in fog weather: the sky dome is white but the PMREM environment still shows a blue sky, so the pool (and any glossy material) reflects saturated blue against the fog.
issues.evidence: shots/critic/environment/r2fog.png pool (500-700, 335-410) saturated blue vs white sky; showcase pool is roughness 0.13 MeshStandard, so this is the env probe, not planar reflection.
issues.suggestion: Apply the same fog-dissolve mix in the envMode branch of the sky shader (same transmittance curve as the main pass) and force probe.refresh() on weather set, including URL-driven weather at init. Verify pool luminance/hue within ~10% of the sky above it.

issues.description: Showcase tower windows at night are a uniform 100%-lit bright lattice that reads as programmer art and dominates the night frame.
issues.suggestion: Randomise per-window on/off (~60% lit) with warm/cool colour temperature variation and emissive 0.3-1.0; keep the window texture at correct 3 m floor pitch.

issues.description: Noon frame is slightly washed and flat: low ground contrast, pale grass, and no discernible drifting cloud shadow on the plaza despite visible cloud cover.
issues.suggestion: Pull noon exposure ~0.15 EV, deepen the hemisphere ground term, and confirm cloudShadowFraction > 0 with the R8 map actually darkening the plaza by 20-40% under the visible deck.

issues.description: Milky Way is not readable at 21:03; stars are faint pinpricks only.
issues.suggestion: Check the star cube is not washed by the moonlit sky term; scale the Milky Way boost by (1 - moonIllumination*moonUp) and by cloud transmittance so it appears in clear gaps.

strengths: Fog at noon is a convincing milky high-key medium: towers, trees and terrain dissolve correctly with distance and exposure stays daylight.
Night is dark blue, not black: moonlit grey-blue clouds, stars, warm lamp pools with soft ground falloff.
Soft cascaded shadows with clean penumbra, no acne or peter-panning on the shader balls.

Complete contract: all engine sun/hemisphere/fog/fog-height/environment/exposure/material-hook/sun-modulation/wetness calls present, world.env fully published, env.api exposes weather/latitude/wind/sky sampling.
0 console errors and 0 warnings across all shots; 92-358 fps, 1200-1560 draw calls, 2.8-4.5M tris; time and weather jumps snap on the first frame.
